title: Sequencing a digital scholarly editing / TEI curriculum
query: In what sequence should a digital scholarly editing curriculum teach cataloguing, transcription, normalization, collation, TEI markup, annotation, and publication, and what evidence supports that ordering?

results.title: The Scholarly Edition Workflow: Tradition Meets Technology
results.authors_venue_year: The Scholarly Edition Workflow: Tradition Meets TechnologyKM Penner - Artificial Intelligence for Bible Translation and …, 2026 - books.google.comDescribes a structured workflow mirroring the seven-stage traditional process of creating a scholarly edition, detailing steps from manuscript identification and transcription to normalization, and culminating in a final project.Course Methodology: Details the sequence of activities in an undergraduate course, starting with manuscript identification (catalog information), proceeding to transcription and reconciliation, followed by normalizing, and ultimately presenting the final output using TEI Publisher.TEI Output Sequence: Explains that the final output of the course was a TEI conformant XML file that included a TEI header with catalog information, a diplomatic transcription, a normalized text with textual variants, lemmas, and parsings, a translation, and comments, suggesting this is the publication sequence.Save Cite Related articles  [PDF] ubiquitypress.comCheck for full text @ X

results.title: Epigraphers and encoders: strategies for teaching and learning digital epigraphy
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] Epigraphers and encoders: strategies for teaching and learning digital epigraphyG Bodard, S Stoyanova - Digital Classics Outside the Echo …, 2016 - ubiquitypress.comDiscusses a change in the EpiDoc training workshop sequence, which shifted from introducing detailed text markup first, then monument description markup, to starting with an overview of the entire document structure, followed by monument description and detailed text markup last.Evidence for Sequencing: Explains the evidence supporting the revised teaching strategy, noting that starting with the document structure and monument description proved clearer and more comprehensible to students, immediately demonstrating that the EpiDoc document structure mirrors that of a traditional epigraphic publication.Placement of Indexing: Describes the placement of lemmatizing and indexing at the end of the EpiDoc training, illustrating that the rigorous intellectual effort of indexing in a traditional project is changed but not replaced by an automated process in the digital workflow, which follows the logical progression of an epigraphic project.Save Cite Cited by 33 Related articles All 18 versions  View as HTML

results.title: Digitization education
results.authors_venue_year: [HTML][HTML] Digitization educationM Dahlström, A Doracic - D-Lib Magazine, 2009 - dlib.orgDescribes the curriculum of a cultural heritage digitization course that includes teaching the "whole digitization chain" from project planning to output/publishing on the web.Sequence of Instruction: Outlines the pedagogical sequence of instruction as project planning, text and image capture (scanning, OCR, or transcription), editing/management (image editing, XML text encoding, annotation, database management), and output/publishing on the web (XSL transformation).Pedagogical Support: Explains the pedagogical approach that requires students to produce different text transcription level outputs (diplomatic and normalized text) from one source by using TEI and XSLT, enhancing flexibility and reusability.Save Cite Cited by 32 Related articles All 7 versions  Cached [PDF] oapen.orgCheck for full text @ X

results.title: Remodeling the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) Workshop
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] Remodeling the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI) WorkshopJ Russell, MI Maza, LM Cenci… - Digital Humanities …, 2023 - library.oapen.orgDescribes a graduate course where students first focused on histories and theories of editing early modern plays, followed by practical matters such as establishing and mediating the playtext and editorial interventions using XML/TEI.Pedagogical Rationale: Suggests that working through data models before getting to encoding helps students articulate assumptions about the text structure, which facilitates learning the conceptual bases of digital scholarly editing.Encoding Training Focus: Explains that the initial training for graduate students included an introduction to XML and TEI Guidelines, focusing on core elements and the drama module, to enable them to complete the text encoding task.Save Cite Related articles All 6 versions  View as HTML [PDF] hal.science

results.title: Digital scholarly editing: Theories, models and methods
results.authors_venue_year: [BOOK][B] Digital scholarly editing: Theories, models and methodsE Pierazzo - 2016 - books.google.comSuggests the typical workflow of preparing an edition begins with choosing the object to edit, followed by editorial work, then post-production and publication, and finally, long-term issues.Textbook Timeline: Proposes a curriculum timeline that guides the reader along the ideal ‘textbook’ timeline of preparing an edition, starting from the elaboration of abstract models of the objects being edited.Theoretical Examination: Aims to examine the theoretical and methodological issues and problems that emerge during the stages of digital scholarly editing when applying computational techniques and methods.Save Cite Cited by 401 Related articles All 11 versions  No full text available [HTML] openbookpublishers.com

results.title: Hands-on teaching digital humanities: a didactic analysis of a summer school course on digital editing
results.authors_venue_year: Hands-on teaching digital humanities: a didactic analysis of a summer school course on digital editingM Rehbein, C Fritze - Digital Humanities Pedagogy. Open Book Publishers …, 2012 - JSTORDiscusses the rationale behind a week-long summer school course on digital editing, including its learning objectives, content, methods, and tools.Sequential Workflow: Explains that the course used a "learning-by-project" approach where the results from one phase of editorial work built the basis for the next phase, suggesting a sequential workflow for transcription and encoding as initial steps.Transcription and Encoding Definition: Defines transcription as transforming texts into machine-readable format (sequence of characters) and encoding (using TEI P5 Guidelines) as the subsequent step of enriching this raw data with structural and semantic features.Save Cite Cited by 43 Related articles All 4 versions  [PDF] kcl.ac.uk

results.title: The Making of Empirical Knowledge: Recipes, Craft, and Scholarly Communication
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] The Making of Empirical Knowledge: Recipes, Craft, and Scholarly CommunicationPH Smith, TH Uchacz, N Rosenkranz, CC Sabel - 2020 - kclpure.kcl.ac.ukDescribes a pedagogical initiative, the Making and Knowing Project, which focused on creating a digital critical edition of a 16th-century manuscript, blending collaborative scholarship, digital humanities, and material practices.Initial Encoding and Transcription: Explains that the first stage of the digital critical edition process involved paleography workshops where graduate students gained skills by transcribing, translating, and encoding the manuscript.Workflow Sequence: Details the sequence of outcomes from the paleography workshops, which produced a finalized diplomatic transcription, a normalized transcription, and an English translation, all marked-up using a custom XML tag set derived from the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI).Save Cite Cited by 1 Related articles All 9 versions  View as HTML [PDF] openedition.org
